groundNote: which ground the close view draws (set.ts): main is the ground that main draws (convect.ts over the plate), lab is the lab's ground (lab/ground.ts with its far level on the globe's face). The anchor below (stage.toBody, globe, twin; plan.ts params.spot) is main's. The lab's ground wants the anchor in anchorForLab: the place 0.14 degrees west and 0.71 south over the map, where the map's knot lies under the lab's spot.
measured: The limb of the approved close image is a conic in the picture. With the lens of the terrain view (vfov below, 16:9) every limb point is a ray from the camera, and the rays of a sphere limb lie on a cone round the nadir. assets-src/sun/terrain/fit.py fitted that cone to the limb read from two clean takes registered to the approved image (the direction of the nadir and the half angle, src/stops/sun/terrain.json down and alphaDeg). The half angle gives the dip and the height: dip = 90 - alpha, height = 1 / cos(dip) - 1. Pitch and roll are the angles of the camera axes to the nadir. The spot is the centre of the umbra (terrain.json spot), its ray met with the sphere. Heading: the far direction through the spot is the north of the globe at the spot (dive.headingDeg 0), so the aim has the bearing below. assets-src/sun/place/limb.py reads the limb again from the approved image itself and gives the residual below; assets-src/sun/place/solve.ts wrote this file.

limbResidual.note: the fitted limb lies on the top of the bright fringe; the photosphere edge between the loop feet sits about 2 percent of the frame height under it

stage.note: a stage point p is the body point toBody * (p - centre) / radius; body axes are the world axes of the orbit view at the middle of the hold, the globe turns about its axis from there

globe.note: spot and north in body axes; mapSpot and mapNorth in the axes of the globe map (the mesh turned back by its fit), where the patch levels are laid: east = Y x mapSpot, north = mapSpot x east

twin.note: the camera of the approved image on the unit sphere, body axes; the terrain view passes through it at frame 90

onGlobe.note: on the globe's side of the rise the ground of the close view lies on the globe's own ball and the ball is drawn under it. away: the ground gives way to the globe's own face by the distance from the eye (radii of the ball, even steps in the logarithm), the far side of the ball first and the place under the eye last; it begins where the map is about 1.4 times enlarged in the picture. red: before it leaves, the light of the far ground is reddened by the way to the eye toward the colour of the globe's face (tint at the most, over these distances in radii). heights are heights of the eye in radii, each a smooth step in the logarithm of the height during the rise: surface only takes the ground's pass away once away has let all but a hundredth of it go under the eye; (the arcade, the jets and the glow at the limb leave by distances, see far); corona and sky are where the corona, the prominences and the far sky come in: the corona is a law of the sky's plane (corona.ts reads its picture by the distance at which a look passes the ball's centre), under a height of about 0.3 it shows a band and arcs, so it begins there and takes the rest of the rise; tidy, spot, field and haze (and capDeg, fade, lowLod, spotKeep) belong to the globe's own drawing of the place, which is switched off (globe.place is called with 0): they drive nothing in the picture; carry is the turn of the film's sky from the close view's frame to the hold's (plan.ts skyCarryShare hands it to the engine): whole close view's below the first height, whole hold's above the second, which is the height the rise ends at; the first lies above the height of the change of view (0.118 at frame 205), so both sides of it show the same sky
onGlobe.gasNote: gas: the share of the corona's and the prominences' light that the lens holds beside the bright ground, by the eye's height alone (radii of the ball), the same law down and up and in every segment (set.ts gasAt). Under the height 'from' it is the constant 'low': the glow from inside that the surface view holds, brighter toward the horizon by the look's angle (corona.ts), the same at every frame of the close view (the eye stands between 0.045 and 0.057 radii there). From 'from' to 'to' it rises to 1 by a smooth step in the logarithm of the height, no slope at either end; 'to' lies under the height of the hold, so the hold and the travel stand at the whole share. MAIL 1415: with from at 0.03 the rise held 0.36 of the gas at frame 212 and 0.61 at 221, a wide grey veil over the stars while the ground still filled the frame; with from at 0.3 the share is the floor up to frame 216, 0.097 at 221, 0.242 at 225, 0.429 at 229, 0.620 at 233, 0.874 at 240, 0.980 at 247, 1 at 256 (assets-src/sun/place/gasshare.ts). The gas itself is seated on the ball at every height, in the close view in the stage's frame as the arcade is.
onGlobe.skyAimNote: skyAim: the aim of the film's sky in the close view (plan.ts skyAim.terrain). MAIL 1427 (a): set so that the Milky Way runs from the upper left of the frame down behind the arcade to the limb, where the approved close picture has it (found by assets-src/sun/place/skysolve.ts from two places of the band read in the approved picture). What it costs: this aim and the hold's stand 53.519 degrees apart. The aim before (71.83722, 136.56647, 27.5002, found by onesky.ts) stood 13.879 apart, gave the sky no turn of its own against the Sun's body (0.518 degrees a frame at the most) and left the sky behind the arch nearly black. With this aim the sky turns against the body by the eye's height alone over heights.carry, by at most 1.998 degrees a frame (frame 224); its step in the picture is at most 1.011 degrees a frame (frame 223). Main's aim: 2.516 and 3.325. Numbers by assets-src/sun/place/skystep-aim.ts with the aim as its arguments.

closeSky.note: the light of the film's sky that the lens holds in the close view, beside the bright ground (the engine's terrainSkyGlow, with its star law of a surface view): 1 is the open sky of the orbit. It returns to 1 by height alone, over heights.sky

far.note: distances from the eye to the thing's own place in radii of the ball, each a smooth step in the logarithm of the distance, one law at every frame (the close view holds nothing as far away as a range begins: the eye is 0.152 to 0.188 radii from the arcade's place there and at most 0.343 from the limb, and no jet in sight stands farther than the limb). strands: the arcade's faint haze and thin strands are cut (loopsCut) over this distance from the eye to the middle between its feet, loops: the arcade leaves over this one. jets: a jet leaves over this distance from the eye to its own foot. glow: the glow at the limb leaves over this distance from the eye to the limb.

rise.note: the rise is one path in the frame of the turning globe: height runs in equal ratios from the close glide (coasting to rest over coast seconds, carried with the globe) to the hold run back in time, rate eased over the first easeIn and the last easeOut of the segment; the direction from the centre turns in step with height, the camera keeps the spot by a look at it and turns from the close framing to the hold framing with the same progress, the lens too. at, dissolveFrames and placeFrames are the handover times of cut/HANDOVER.md E1: T sits at frame 205 (at 0.28): the two sides draw the same picture there (the ground laid on the globe is the close ground, nothing of the globe is in the picture yet), and from 207 on the first far ground is 0.6 radii from the eye and begins to give way to the globe's face, which only the globe's side can show. Since the stop left handover.ownPath (config/showcase.json) the rise is flown by the engine's one move with law (pace, turn, liftPower: the set handover_engineer searched for the Sun); easeIn, easeOut, coast, steps and turn belong to the stop's own path, which the engine no longer asks for; skyFrames 0: the close view's sky leaves by the height of the lens (the plan's skyShare, heights onGlobe.heights.sky) and not by the clock

bend.note: the bend of the surface view into its rise (d196), the engine's own (src/director/bend.ts): from this second of the surface view on the eye keeps the share of its height it flies a second and turns its way through acrossDeg (azimuth from its level way, 90 to its right; elevation) by turnDeg, so it leaves the way the rise carries on. hold: the share of the bend's shift of the spot in the picture that the lens takes out by turning with it. Frames 0 to 95 keep their camera

drift.note: the drift of the surface view (MAIL 836 point 5 iv): on top of its glide the eye slides to its right, level over the ground, from side stage units left of the glide at frame 0 into the glide itself at frame 90, by (1 - t over the time of frame 90) to the power: fastest at the start, eased out to no speed and no change of speed at frame 90, so the near ground passes faster than the far ground and the horizon. From frame 90 on the camera is the glide's own (the bend and the rise keep their path)
